parsed.why: Protective state: gender-identity anti-discrimination law, hate-crime coverage, shield law, facilities access protected, and a 2026 court order favouring trans youth care. Offset by national passport/entry exposure and a pending ballot measure, plus the state's own dependence on federal funding, so it sits in reduced risk, below the parent average's comparator tier.

Gender identity removed from state civil-rights statutes in 2025; a 2026 law bars localities from stronger protections; no remedy for refused service. Statewide school-facilities rule binds everyone on school grounds including visitors, and birth-certificate rule governs multiperson facilities. Documented hostility with no recourse places it in high risk.

Facility bans enacted 2024-25, birth-sex marker rules after 2026 law, a 2025 supreme court ruling against name change, and documented birth-sex prison-related harm. Gender identity absent from state hate-crime and anti-discrimination law; a religious-refusal statute enables service refusal. Murder rate above baseline with a 2017 killing unrecorded later. High risk, above the bottom.

Among the most protective tier: statewide gender-identity protections, hate-crime coverage, shield law for visitors seeking care, X markers, and gender-neutral facilities. Remains exposed to national passport, entry and custody rules, and county-level sports exclusion, but state operation is strong, placing it at low risk.

State civil-rights coverage with enforcement shown (2026 conviction for striking a trans woman) and hate-crime enhancements. Offset by 2024-25 youth care bans, surgery requirement for birth certificate change, a sports ban with stay, and a state reputation for low safety. Elevated risk.
